The single-square classification, the aligned charge  $-o/2$ , the freezing argument—including exactly two outward-matched corners—and the  $8\times8$  neutral obstacle all survive its correction. Their component calculations use  $s=0$ .The review below follows from the written arguments and direct exact inspection of the specified configurations.1. Required correction: the tile-charge identityFor a deficient tile, matching endpoints partition into three classes:
$$p=2h+s+d.$$
Together with  $t+p+b=4$  and the stated definition  $r=2-t-h$ , this gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac d2-r
&=\frac{p-2h-s}{2}-(2-t-h)\\
&=\frac{2t+p-4-s}{2}\\
&=\boxed{\frac{t-b-s}{2}}.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus the supplied equality
$$\frac d2-r=\frac{t-b+s}{2}$$
holds precisely when  $s=0$ .This discrepancy occurs in feasible single-terminal configurations. For example, use zero-based coordinates in a  $4\times4$  grid, with
$$T=\{(0,2),(1,1),(2,3),(3,2)\},
\qquad
M=\bigl\{\{(1,2),(2,2)\}\bigr\},$$
and all remaining vertices blank. Each endpoint has its matching mate and two selected neighbors; every selected vertex has exactly one occupied neighbor.The upper-right tile has labels  $TB/PB$ , while its endpoint’s mate lies in the saturated lower-right tile  $PT/TB$ . Consequently, the upper-right tile has
$$(t,p,b,h,s,d,r)=(1,1,2,0,1,0,1),$$
and therefore
$$\frac d2-r=-1,
\qquad
\frac{t-b+s}{2}=0.$$
The recommended repair preserves the intended positive- $s$  charge:
$$\boxed{\rho=\frac d2-r+s=\frac{t-b+s}{2},
\qquad r=2-t-h.}$$
Equivalently, introduce the adjusted residual
$$r_{\mathrm{eff}}=2-t-h-s,
\qquad
\rho=\frac d2-r_{\mathrm{eff}}.$$
Keeping  $\rho=d/2-r$  instead requires the formula  $(t-b-s)/2$ . These two conventions differ globally by
$$\sum_{\text{deficient tiles}}s.$$
That distinction matters for the eventual global inequality and for source estimates involving  $s>0$ . All receiver calculations and the displayed neutral obstacle agree under both conventions.2.
